completion_proofs.artifact_or_reference: Bank credit and, where selected/required, annuity or periodic-withdrawal contract.
completion_proofs.validation_method: Reconcile PRAN, amount, claimant and product/withdrawal record; a status or redemption event alone is insufficient.

completion_proofs.name: Company-confirmed IEPF investor record
completion_proofs.artifact_or_reference: Company/RTA confirmation of original holder, folio/demat, shares and amounts.
completion_proofs.validation_method: Match company filing and claimant's record.

completion_proofs.name: IEPF-5 SRN and acknowledgement
completion_proofs.artifact_or_reference: MCA SRN, acknowledgement and generated indemnity.
completion_proofs.validation_method: Match claimant, company and claimed shares/amounts.

completion_proofs.name: Company/bank online verification report status
completion_proofs.artifact_or_reference: MCA/company verification report and completeness/deficiency status.
completion_proofs.validation_method: Match SRN, company nodal officer, report date and whether the Authority received a complete report.

completion_proofs.name: IEPF shares or amount refund proof
completion_proofs.artifact_or_reference: Demat credit and/or bank credit linked to SRN.
completion_proofs.validation_method: Reconcile ISIN/quantity/amount, claimant accounts and SRN; Authority disposition without credit is not payment proof.

completion_proofs.name: Account-office route confirmation
completion_proofs.artifact_or_reference: Written/acknowledged confirmation of scheme, nomination, claimant capacity, eligible balance, forms and legal-evidence route.
completion_proofs.validation_method: Match account number, office and current rule; keep SBI SCSS instructions scoped to SBI.
completion_proofs.retention_use: Route selection proof, not submission or payment.

completion_proofs.name: Postal death-claim acknowledgement
completion_proofs.artifact_or_reference: Transaction-office receipt/reference and completed-document date if accepted as complete.
completion_proofs.validation_method: Match scheme/account, claimant and submitted forms; do not infer completeness merely from a receipt.

completion_proofs.name: Postal small-savings payment or closure proof
completion_proofs.artifact_or_reference: Payment advice/bank credit or account closure/transmission record.
completion_proofs.validation_method: Reconcile account, eligible balance and claimant; do not infer heir distribution.
completion_proofs.retention_use: Claim outcome evidence, distinct from receipt.

completion_proofs.name: Official grievance reference
completion_proofs.artifact_or_reference: RBI CMS, SCORES, Bima Bharosa, EPFiGMS, Pension Sahayak, India Post or CPGRAMS reference with action history and dates.
completion_proofs.validation_method: Match the responsible portal, institution, underlying claim, filing date, response level and next deadline.
completion_proofs.retention_use: Grievance tracking only; not claim settlement.

claims.statement: The verified official corpus provides asset-class-specific discovery routes but no single national search that proves the complete set of a deceased person's covered financial assets.
claims.subject: Cross-asset discovery
claims.applicability: This pack's covered asset classes and sources only; negative inference from route boundaries, not a claim that no private or future service exists.
claims.locator: Comparative scope of each official asset-class route; none states it is a complete cross-asset registry.

claims.statement: UDGAM lets registered users search unclaimed deposits transferred to the DEA Fund across participating banks.
claims.subject: Bank discovery
claims.applicability: UDGAM participating-bank/DEA-Fund records, not every bank asset.
claims.locator: UDGAM FAQ questions 1-3 and RBI launch release.

claims.statement: UDGAM search uses account-holder name, selected bank and one of PAN, driving licence, voter ID, passport number or date of birth, with address permitted where none is available.
claims.subject: UDGAM inputs
claims.applicability: Individual user search described in RBI FAQ.
claims.locator: UDGAM FAQ questions 5-6.

claims.statement: UDGAM does not receive or settle claims; the claimant must approach the respective bank, using the bank claim-process link and UDRN where available.
claims.subject: UDGAM boundary
claims.applicability: All UDGAM matches.
claims.locator: UDGAM FAQ questions 7-9.

claims.statement: Deposit balances unoperated or unclaimed for ten years are transferred by banks to the Depositor Education and Awareness Fund, while claims continue through the bank.
claims.subject: Unclaimed bank deposit lifecycle
claims.applicability: Covered bank deposit accounts under the DEA Fund Scheme.
claims.locator: DEA Fund FAQ questions 1, 3 and 5.

claims.statement: For a valid nominee or survivor claim, a bank may discharge itself after verifying death and claimant identity and absence of a restraining court order, while making clear that the recipient receives as trustee for legal heirs.
claims.subject: Bank nominee/survivor payment
claims.applicability: Accounts with valid nomination or survivorship mandate and no restraining court order.
claims.locator: Paragraph 20.1.1.

claims.statement: Banks should not insist on succession certificate, probate, letters of administration, indemnity or surety from a valid survivor/nominee regardless of account amount.
claims.subject: Bank nominee/survivor documents
claims.applicability: Valid survivor/nominee claims under the cited RBI instruction.
claims.locator: Paragraph 20.1.2.

claims.statement: Where there is no nominee or survivorship mandate, banks set their own simplified-procedure threshold based on risk; the RBI instruction does not create one national monetary threshold.
claims.subject: Bank no-nomination route
claims.applicability: No-nomination/no-survivorship deceased-depositor claims.
claims.locator: Paragraph 20.2.

claims.statement: Banks should settle valid survivor/nominee claims within 15 days from receipt, subject to proof of death and suitable claimant identification.
claims.subject: Bank nominee/survivor timeline
claims.applicability: Complete valid survivor/nominee claims under the cited RBI instruction.
claims.locator: RBI paragraph 20.6; SBI 2025 deceased-account claims section.

claims.statement: SBI's 2025 policy describes a deceased-claim digital intake with KYC/death uploads, selected branch and CRM case ID tracking.
claims.subject: Bank channel example
claims.applicability: SBI only; not generalized to other banks.
claims.locator: Deceased deposit accounts and Centralized Deceased Claim portal section, pages 43-44 in the PDF.

claims.statement: Under RBI's current Integrated Ombudsman framework, the complainant first approaches the regulated entity and may approach RBI after an unsatisfactory response or no response for 30 days, subject to the applicable maintainability/time rules; filing is free and trackable on CMS.
claims.subject: Bank grievance
claims.applicability: Complaints covered by the RBI Integrated Ombudsman Scheme FAQ effective 1 July 2026.
claims.locator: FAQ sections on prior complaint, maintainability, filing, cost and tracking.

claims.statement: A maintainable RBI Ombudsman complaint must be lodged within 90 days from expiry of the regulated entity's applicable reply period or from its last communication, whichever is later.
claims.subject: RBI Ombudsman filing period
claims.applicability: Complaints under the RBI Integrated Ombudsman Scheme FAQ effective 1 July 2026; this is not an estate-claim limitation period.
claims.locator: FAQ section on the time limit for filing a complaint.

claims.statement: The RBI FAQ uses 30-day periods for a complainant's acceptance of an award, regulated-entity compliance or appeal, and an eligible complainant appeal; only the stated sufficient-cause extension applies.
claims.subject: RBI Ombudsman post-order period
claims.applicability: The actual award/order and party's appeal right control; the pack does not treat every closure as appealable.
claims.locator: FAQ sections on award acceptance, compliance and appeal.

claims.statement: SEBI's 2026 transmission bands are: physical securities or AMC statement-of-account units per entity/AMC, QTP up to ₹10,000 and simplified up to ₹10 lakh; demat per beneficial-owner account, QTP up to ₹30,000 and simplified up to ₹30 lakh.
claims.subject: SEBI transmission value bands
claims.applicability: Listed securities and AMC units covered by the circular, effective 22 August 2026.
claims.locator: Circular pages 2 and 6, QTP and simplified thresholds/table.

claims.statement: For death of a joint holder, the surviving joint holder supplies only the death certificate without KYC, indemnity or undertaking, subject to nothing contrary in the company's articles.
claims.subject: SEBI surviving joint-holder route
claims.applicability: Covered joint holdings under the 2026 circular.
claims.locator: Circular joint-holder provision.

claims.statement: A registered nominee receives transmitted securities or units as trustee for the legal heirs and submits the specified transmission form, claimant CML, verifiable death certificate and certificate/SOA where applicable.
claims.subject: SEBI nominee route
claims.applicability: Covered nominee claims under the 2026 circular.
claims.locator: Circular nominee documentation and trustee provision.

claims.statement: Without nomination, SEBI's 2026 framework uses distinct QTP, simplified and above-threshold evidence routes, including defined immediate-relative proof for QTP, notarised indemnity/NOCs or family settlement for simplified cases, and specified will/state-legal-heir/court evidence combinations above threshold.
claims.subject: SEBI no-nomination transmission documents
claims.applicability: Undisputed covered claims without a valid nomination; actual band/value and state formalities must be confirmed.
claims.locator: Circular no-nomination QTP, simplified and above-threshold provisions and annexed forms.

claims.statement: Covered intermediaries must process transmission within 21 calendar days after receiving all required documents.
claims.subject: SEBI transmission timeline
claims.applicability: Complete, covered, undisputed transmission requests under the 2026 circular.
claims.locator: Circular processing timeline provision.

claims.statement: The receiving entity must acknowledge receipt and identify missing/incomplete documents; delay or rejection reasons must be communicated in writing, and additional documents beyond the framework require written reasons.
claims.subject: SEBI acknowledgement and rejection
claims.applicability: Covered transmission requests under the 2026 circular.
claims.locator: Circular acknowledgement, additional-document and rejection provisions.

claims.statement: The SEBI simplified transmission framework does not apply to disputed or competing claims, which proceed through appropriate legal/judicial handling.
claims.subject: SEBI dispute boundary
claims.applicability: Competing/disputed claims.
claims.locator: Circular scope/exclusion for disputed claims.

claims.statement: MITRA is an industry searchable database operated by CAMS and KFin QRTAs to help investors or rightful legal claimants trace inactive or unclaimed mutual-fund folios.
claims.subject: Mutual-fund discovery
claims.applicability: Inactive/unclaimed mutual-fund folios in the SEBI circular's scope.
claims.locator: Circular paragraphs 1-5.

claims.statement: MITRA defines an inactive folio as one with no investor-initiated financial or non-financial transaction for ten years while a unit balance remains; a search result still requires AMC/RTA transmission.
claims.subject: MITRA scope boundary
claims.applicability: MITRA records and resulting AMC/RTA process.
claims.locator: Circular definition and platform purpose, paragraphs 2-5.

claims.statement: AMFI hosts an August 2026 transmission-document matrix and forms reflecting the current SEBI framework for death of a unit holder.
claims.subject: Mutual-fund forms
claims.applicability: Form selection support; actual claim is processed by AMC/RTA.
claims.locator: Death of Unit Holder page, August 2026 matrix/forms.

claims.statement: SCORES requires the investor first to take the grievance to the entity and then supports registration, tracking and two review levels.
claims.subject: Securities grievance
claims.applicability: SEBI-regulated entity service grievances.
claims.locator: SCORES home and FAQ workflow.

claims.statement: On SCORES, the regulated entity must resolve the grievance and upload its Action Taken Report within 21 calendar days.
claims.subject: SCORES entity response
claims.applicability: SEBI-regulated entity grievances registered on SCORES.
claims.locator: SCORES FAQ, grievance-redress flow and entity ATR period.

claims.statement: A complainant dissatisfied with an ATR may request the applicable SCORES review within 15 calendar days; the Designated Body first review is due within 10 calendar days where triggered.
claims.subject: SCORES review windows
claims.applicability: First and second review stages described by the live SCORES FAQ; portal auto-escalation applies where stated.
claims.locator: SCORES FAQ, first-review and second-review workflow.

claims.statement: A SCORES complaint should normally be lodged within one year from the cause of action, with SEBI retaining the FAQ-stated discretion to accept delay.
claims.subject: SCORES complaint period
claims.applicability: Service-grievance lodging; not a limitation rule for inheritance or the underlying asset claim.
claims.locator: SCORES FAQ, complaint time limit.

claims.statement: No current primary source in this research establishes a public cross-DP/cross-issuer deceased-claimant search for all listed securities.
claims.subject: Securities discovery gap
claims.applicability: Unknown DP/issuer/folio cases; not a claim that no future/private search exists.
claims.locator: The transmission circular governs known records and does not provide a universal discovery service.

claims.statement: IRDAI's Bima Bharosa unclaimed-amount page lists insurer-specific routes rather than receiving a single cross-insurer death claim.
claims.subject: Insurance discovery
claims.applicability: Unclaimed-amount discovery leads.
claims.locator: Unclaimed Amount page insurer list/links.

claims.statement: LIC's current first-party route directs the legally entitled person to the servicing branch and lists Claim Form A, death evidence, original policy/assignment records and possible case/product additions.
claims.subject: Insurance death-claim example
claims.applicability: LIC example only; not a universal insurer checklist or entitlement rule.
claims.locator: Download Forms, Death Claims section; page updated 27 April 2026.

claims.statement: The Bima Bharosa FAQ instructs policyholders to complain to the insurer first and allows IRDAI escalation if the insurer does not resolve the grievance within 15 days, with token-based tracking.
claims.subject: Insurance grievance
claims.applicability: Insurance service grievances in Bima Bharosa scope.
claims.locator: FAQ questions on when/how to complain and tracking.

claims.statement: A life-insurance death claim must be settled within 15 days from claim intimation unless investigation is required, in which case the period is 45 days from claim intimation.
claims.subject: Life-insurance death-claim timeline
claims.applicability: Life-insurance death claims under the IRDAI Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024.
claims.locator: Circular PDF pages 108 and 152, death-claim TAT and Schedule A.

claims.statement: For delay beyond the applicable life death-claim TAT, the insurer must pay interest at bank rate plus 2% per annum from claim intimation until payment, suo motu.
claims.subject: Life-insurance delayed-claim interest
claims.applicability: Delay under the 15-day or 45-day death-claim TAT; the pack does not calculate the amount or assume a particular bank rate.
claims.locator: Circular PDF page 108, delay-interest provision.

claims.statement: A life claim must not be rejected or closed merely for want of documents or delayed intimation, and repudiation requires legally tenable evidence; insurers must state required documents in the policy and on their website.
claims.subject: Life-insurance deficiency and rejection controls
claims.applicability: Life-insurance claims under the 2024 Master Circular; it does not waive genuinely required policy/identity evidence.
claims.locator: Circular PDF pages 107-108 and 146.

claims.statement: Before paying a life death claim, the insurer must check any valid assignment and outstanding policy loan; only the balance is paid to the nominee where those claims apply.
claims.subject: Life-policy assignment and loan boundary
claims.applicability: Policies with a valid assignment or outstanding loan; amounts must be obtained from the insurer.
claims.locator: Circular PDF page 108, assignment/outstanding-loan check.

claims.statement: An insurer must acknowledge a grievance immediately and communicate action or decision within 14 days; the 2024 Master Circular points to the Insurance Ombudsman if the grievance remains unresolved for 30 days or the decision is unacceptable.
claims.subject: Insurance grievance timeline
claims.applicability: Insurance grievances under Schedule A of the 2024 Master Circular; Ombudsman subject-matter and filing eligibility remain case specific.
claims.locator: Circular PDF pages 152-153, Schedule A grievance rows.

claims.statement: Insurance Act section 39(7) gives beneficial-entitlement treatment to a nominee who is a parent, spouse or child (or a combination), subject to the section's qualifications, creditor rights, assignments and statutory exceptions.
claims.subject: Life-insurance nominee effect
claims.applicability: Only a nomination within section 39 and the statutory relationships/conditions; no cross-asset nominee-ownership inference.
claims.locator: Insurance Act, 1938, section 39(7), read with section 39 qualifications and exceptions.

claims.statement: EPFO identifies Form 20 for claiming provident-fund dues after a member's death by the applicable nominee, beneficiary or legal heir.
claims.subject: EPF death claim
claims.applicability: Deceased EPF member claim, subject to claimant/member record.
claims.locator: Which Claim Form, death cases; Form 20 instructions.

claims.statement: EPFO identifies Form 10D for an applicable family-pension claim after member death, with claimant category depending on family/nomination/dependent-parent facts.
claims.subject: EPS death pension
claims.applicability: Only where pension claimant and service conditions are met.
claims.locator: Which Claim Form, death cases; Form 20 instructions discussion of Form 10D claimant categories.

claims.statement: EPFO identifies Form 5IF for an EDLI benefit claim where the member died while in service, subject to the applicable establishment/coverage route.
claims.subject: EDLI death claim
claims.applicability: Covered death while in service; not every EPF member death.
claims.locator: Which Claim Form, death cases; Form 20 instructions note on Form 5IF.

claims.statement: An EPF claim complete in all respects and submitted with the requisite documents must be settled and the benefit paid within 20 days from receipt by the Commissioner.
claims.subject: EPF complete-claim timeline
claims.jurisdiction: India under Employees' Provident Funds Scheme, 2026
claims.applicability: Complete claims only; the period does not assert completeness where EPFO identifies a supported deficiency.
claims.locator: G.S.R. 525(E), paragraph 54(7), PDF page 94. G.S.R. 703(E) checked in full; it does not amend paragraph 54(7).

claims.statement: Where an EPF claim has a deficiency, EPFO must communicate the deficiency to the claimant within 20 days from receipt of the application.
claims.subject: EPF deficiency-notice timeline
claims.jurisdiction: India under Employees' Provident Funds Scheme, 2026
claims.applicability: Claims in which a deficiency is found.
claims.locator: G.S.R. 525(E), paragraph 54(8), PDF page 94. G.S.R. 703(E) checked in full; it does not amend paragraph 54(8).

claims.statement: If the Commissioner fails without sufficient cause to settle a complete EPF claim within 20 days, penal interest at 12% per annum may be charged on the benefit amount for delay beyond that period and deducted from the Commissioner's salary.
claims.subject: EPF conditional delay remedy
claims.jurisdiction: India under Employees' Provident Funds Scheme, 2026
claims.applicability: Only delay beyond 20 days on a claim complete in all respects, with no sufficient cause; the scheme says 'may be charged', so the pack does not treat interest as automatic.
claims.locator: G.S.R. 525(E), paragraph 54(9), PDF page 94. G.S.R. 703(E) checked in full; it does not amend paragraph 54(9).

claims.statement: An EPS claim complete in all respects and submitted with the requisite documents must be settled and the benefit paid within 20 days from receipt by the Commissioner.
claims.subject: EPS complete-claim timeline
claims.applicability: Complete claims only; pension eligibility remains separately conditional.
claims.locator: G.S.R. 527(E), paragraph 17(1), PDF page 55. G.S.R. 704(E) corrections to page 55 lines 23 and 25 concern paragraph 15 references, not paragraph 17(1).

claims.statement: Where an EPS claim has a deficiency, it must be recorded in writing and communicated to the applicant within 20 days from receipt of the application.
claims.subject: EPS deficiency-notice timeline
claims.applicability: Claims in which a deficiency is found.
claims.locator: G.S.R. 527(E), paragraph 17(2), PDF pages 55-56. G.S.R. 704(E) checked in full; it does not amend paragraph 17(2).

claims.statement: If the Commissioner fails without sufficient cause to settle a complete EPS claim within 20 days, interest at 12% per annum may be charged on the benefit amount for delay beyond that period and may be deducted from the Commissioner's salary.
claims.subject: EPS conditional delay remedy
claims.applicability: Only delay beyond 20 days on a claim complete in all respects, with no sufficient cause; paragraph 17(3) says 'interest' and 'may be charged', not automatic penal interest.
claims.locator: G.S.R. 527(E), paragraph 17(3), PDF page 56. G.S.R. 704(E) checked in full; it does not amend paragraph 17(3).

claims.statement: An EDLI claim complete in all respects and submitted with the requisite documents must be settled and the benefit paid within 20 days from receipt by the Commissioner.
claims.subject: EDLI complete-claim timeline
claims.jurisdiction: India under Employees' Deposit-Linked Insurance Scheme, 2026
claims.applicability: Complete covered EDLI claims only; death-in-service and other coverage conditions remain separate.
claims.locator: G.S.R. 526(E), paragraph 23(3), PDF page 18. G.S.R. 705(E) page 18 correction concerns paragraph 22 claimant wording, not paragraph 23(3).

claims.statement: Where an EDLI claim has a deficiency, it must be recorded in writing and communicated to the applicant within 20 days from receipt of the application.
claims.subject: EDLI deficiency-notice timeline
claims.jurisdiction: India under Employees' Deposit-Linked Insurance Scheme, 2026
claims.applicability: Claims in which a deficiency is found.
claims.locator: G.S.R. 526(E), paragraph 23(4), PDF page 18. G.S.R. 705(E) checked in full; it does not amend paragraph 23(4).

claims.statement: If the Commissioner fails without sufficient cause to settle a complete EDLI claim within 20 days, penal interest at 12% per annum may be charged on the benefit amount for delay beyond that period and deducted from the Commissioner's salary.
claims.subject: EDLI conditional delay remedy
claims.jurisdiction: India under Employees' Deposit-Linked Insurance Scheme, 2026
claims.applicability: Only delay beyond 20 days on a claim complete in all respects, with no sufficient cause; the scheme says 'may be charged', so the pack does not treat interest as automatic.
claims.locator: G.S.R. 526(E), paragraph 23(5), PDF page 18. G.S.R. 705(E) checked in full; it does not amend paragraph 23(5).

claims.statement: EPFO provides EPFiGMS for grievances and asks a claimant to write with the grievance reference if it remains pending for more than 15 days or redressal is unsatisfactory.
claims.subject: EPFO grievance
claims.applicability: EPFiGMS grievances under the cited EPFO contact instruction.
claims.locator: Contact page grievance section.

claims.statement: For a non-government NPS subscriber who dies before exit, the current regulation provides the entire accumulated wealth to nominee/legal heirs as lump sum, with optional periodic withdrawal or annuity; if no nomination exists, it accepts a state competent-authority legal-heir certificate or court succession certificate.
claims.subject: Non-government NPS death exit
claims.applicability: Non-government sector death before exit under regulation 4(1)(c), current through 20 July 2026.
claims.locator: Regulation 4(1)(c), PDF page 10.

claims.statement: For a government-sector death before superannuation, current regulation Schedule I provides: up to ₹8 lakh, a 100% withdrawal option or the standard 20% lump sum/at least 80% annuity; above ₹8 lakh up to ₹12 lakh, up to ₹6 lakh with the balance through the specified systematic-unit-redemption/annuity options or the standard route; above ₹12 lakh, up to 20% lump sum and at least 80% annuity.
claims.subject: Government NPS death-exit bands
claims.applicability: Government-sector death before superannuation under regulation 3(1)(c) and Schedule I Table 1; confirm accumulated pension wealth and claimant option.
claims.locator: Regulation 3(1)(c), current consolidation PDF page 6; Schedule I Table 1, PDF pages 34-35; 2025 amendment regulation 6 at Gazette PDF pages 4-5; NPS Trust death page, government-sector ₹8 lakh boundary.

claims.statement: PFRDA's live government-sector FAQ still states a ₹5 lakh full-withdrawal threshold on death, but the 16 December 2025 amendment, current regulation consolidation and current NPS Trust guidance align at ₹8 lakh.
claims.subject: Government NPS FAQ threshold
claims.applicability: Retained only as a stale-content warning; it does not control the current amount-band classification.
claims.locator: Government-sector FAQ death answer compared with G.S.R. 1149(E), regulation 3(1)(c), Schedule I Table 1 and NPS Trust death page.

claims.statement: The claimant submits the NPS death-withdrawal request to the associated nodal office/POP, which initiates and authorises the online CRA claim based on claimant documents.
claims.subject: NPS death-claim process
claims.applicability: NPS death withdrawals through the applicable intermediary.
claims.locator: Exit NPS procedure and death-claim workflow.

claims.statement: Protean CRA publishes a claimant withdrawal form for death cases among its current NPS forms.
claims.subject: NPS intermediary form
claims.applicability: Only where Protean is the responsible CRA and the live form matches the case.
claims.locator: Forms page, withdrawal by claimant due to death.

claims.statement: PFRDA provides Pension Sahayak as a portal to lodge and track pension/NPS grievances.
claims.subject: NPS grievance
claims.applicability: Service grievances in portal scope.
claims.locator: PFRDA portal grievance/Pension Sahayak link.

claims.statement: In Protean's NPS Lite death-withdrawal SOP, initiation generates an acknowledgement number, rejection requires a reason, and status is available from the next working day; a penny-drop bank rejection can be corrected and resubmitted.
claims.subject: Protean NPS Lite acknowledgement and rejection
claims.applicability: Only the Protean NPS Lite SOP version 1.3 workflow; not every CRA or NPS sector.
claims.locator: SOP PDF pages 17, 20-21, acknowledgement, rejection reason and status/penny-drop steps.

claims.statement: After nodal authorisation in Protean NPS Lite, the claim is considered in the next settlement cycle, redemption occurs on the next working day (T+1), and fund transfer occurs within two working days after redemption.
claims.subject: Protean NPS Lite settlement timing
claims.applicability: Only valid authorised death-withdrawal requests under the cited SOP; no general NPS processing clock.
claims.locator: SOP PDF page 22, settlement-cycle, redemption and fund-transfer steps.

claims.statement: Protean NPS Lite quality check may hold a case with invalid documents; after a valid nodal response cures the hold, fund transfer is made within three working days.
claims.subject: Protean NPS Lite deficiency hold
claims.applicability: Only the document-quality-check path in the cited SOP; not a universal deficiency-notice clock.
claims.locator: SOP PDF page 22, quality-check hold and post-cure transfer.

claims.statement: A dissatisfied claimant, or one whose grievance remains unresolved for 30 days at the intermediary level, may escalate the NPS grievance to NPS Trust.
claims.subject: NPS grievance level-one period
claims.applicability: PFRDA grievance-redress mechanism after the intermediary complaint.
claims.locator: PFRDA grievance page, level 1 to NPS Trust escalation.

claims.statement: A claimant dissatisfied with NPS Trust's response, or without a response for 21 days at that level, may approach the Ombudsman.
claims.subject: NPS grievance level-two period
claims.applicability: PFRDA grievance-redress mechanism after escalation to NPS Trust.
claims.locator: PFRDA grievance page and FAQ, NPS Trust-to-Ombudsman trigger.

claims.statement: The NPS grievance FAQ sets a 45-day Ombudsman appeal period from the NPS Trust response or, if none, from expiry of the 21-day response period, subject to sufficient-reason discretion.
claims.subject: NPS Ombudsman appeal period
claims.applicability: Eligible NPS grievance appeals; not an underlying withdrawal-claim limitation period.
claims.locator: PFRDA grievance FAQ, Ombudsman appeal eligibility and filing period.

claims.statement: The IEPF-5 kit directs an applicant to file through MCA IEPF services, save the SRN and generated acknowledgement/indemnity, notify the company/bank and follow the stated supporting-document/postal steps.
claims.subject: IEPF refund process
claims.applicability: IEPF-5 claims including claimant/successor cases supported by the form.
claims.locator: IEPF-5 instruction kit, submission and post-submission steps/field instructions.

claims.statement: The IEPF e-verification kit requires the company or bank to submit its online verification report within 30 days of receiving the claim.
claims.subject: IEPF company verification
claims.applicability: IEPF claims requiring company/bank verification.
claims.locator: Online verification instruction kit, verification timeline.

claims.statement: The IEPF Authority must dispose of an application within 60 days after receiving a complete verification report from the company, recording and communicating reasons for any delay.
claims.subject: IEPF Authority disposal timeline
claims.applicability: Rule 7 stage after a complete company verification report; not from the claimant's initial IEPF-5 filing.
claims.locator: IEPF Authority Rules, 2016, rule 7(6).

claims.statement: If required documents remain unsubmitted, or communicated deficiencies remain unrectified, for 90 days after IEPF-5, the Authority may reject only after giving the claimant 30 days to respond.
claims.subject: IEPF deficiency and rejection control
claims.applicability: The rejection paths added by the 2017 amendment; a response opportunity does not guarantee acceptance.
claims.locator: 2017 amendment to rule 7, 90-day document/deficiency period and 30-day response opportunity.

claims.statement: A legal heir, successor, administrator or nominee claiming IEPF-held securities must ensure that the company completes transmission into that claimant's name before filing the refund claim with the Authority.
claims.subject: IEPF transmission-before-refund gate
claims.applicability: Successor/nominee claims under rule 7; the applicable SEBI and company transmission evidence still controls.
claims.locator: IEPF Authority Rules, 2016, rule 7 successor/nominee transmission proviso; SEBI 2026 IEPF applicability.

claims.statement: SEBI's 2026 circular states that the same securities-transmission approach applies to securities transferred to IEPF.
claims.subject: IEPF transmission evidence
claims.applicability: IEPF-held listed securities in the circular's scope.
claims.locator: Circular IEPF applicability provision.

claims.statement: No live current primary source in this research established a reliably navigable cross-company deceased-claimant search for all IEPF-held shares and amounts.
claims.subject: IEPF discovery gap
claims.applicability: Unknown company/folio cases; company records and disclosures remain leads.
claims.locator: IEPF-5 requires company/holder/folio details and is a claim form, not a universal discovery service.

claims.statement: Government Savings Promotion General Rule 15 provides a nominee route using Form 11 and proof of death for the eligible balance after death of the sole or all joint holders.
claims.subject: Central small-savings nominee route
claims.applicability: Accounts governed by General Rule 15 and relevant scheme conditions.

claims.statement: India Post separately identifies a legal-evidence deceased-claim route using probate, letters of administration or a succession certificate, but does not make every listed document interchangeable for every claimant capacity, value band or scheme.
claims.subject: India Post legal-evidence route
claims.applicability: Post-office savings accounts in the live Department of Posts guidance; actual scheme, claimant capacity and instrument must be confirmed.
claims.locator: Post Office Saving Schemes page, deceased-account settlement routes.

claims.statement: Without nomination and where probate, letters of administration or succession certificate has not been produced within six months, General Rule 15 and India Post guidance allow the account office to pay an eligible balance not exceeding ₹5 lakh to a person appearing entitled using Form 11, death proof, passbook/statement and the specified affidavit/disclaimer/indemnity forms.
claims.subject: Central small-savings simplified no-nomination route
claims.applicability: Rule 15 and India Post conditions; no dispute, title adjudication or automatic entitlement is inferred.
claims.locator: General Rule 15(3); India Post deceased-account note for no nomination up to ₹5 lakh; SBI SCSS below-₹5-lakh example.

claims.statement: For a General Rule/India Post account without nomination and an eligible balance above ₹5 lakh, the claimant must use the succession-certificate route with the claim form, death proof and account record.
claims.subject: Central small-savings above-₹5-lakh route
claims.jurisdiction: India Central small savings and India Post
claims.applicability: No-nomination balances above ₹5 lakh under General Rule 15/India Post guidance; does not prescribe the state/court process for obtaining the certificate.
claims.locator: General Rule 15(4); India Post deceased-account note that no-nomination deposits above ₹5 lakh are claimable only through succession certificate.

claims.statement: SBI's SCSS FAQ lists probate, letters of administration, succession certificate or a Tehsildar-issued legal-heir certificate for an SBI SCSS no-nomination claim above ₹5 lakh.
claims.subject: SBI SCSS above-₹5-lakh operating guidance
claims.applicability: SBI SCSS only; the broader actor-specific list must not override or be generalized to the General Rule/India Post no-nomination succession-certificate route.
claims.locator: SBI SCSS FAQ, deceased claim without nomination above ₹5 lakh.

claims.statement: India Post instructs customers to complain at the transaction post office and obtain acknowledgement, then approach the next higher authority and use the online complaint route.
claims.subject: India Post grievance
claims.applicability: India Post service grievances.
claims.locator: Grievance-redress guidelines and escalation sequence.

claims.statement: India Post's Citizen Charter sets a seven-day service standard for settlement of a Post Office Savings Bank deceased claim from receipt of completed documents.
claims.subject: India Post deceased-claim service standard
claims.applicability: Completed Post Office Savings Bank deceased claims; excludes time to obtain succession evidence or cure deficiencies and is not a guaranteed entitlement.
claims.locator: Citizen Charter, Post Office Savings Bank, settlement of deceased claim.

claims.statement: India Post's Citizen Charter provides instantaneous web grievance acknowledgement or seven days by post/other channel, and a 60-day settlement standard, extended to 90 days where investigation is required.
claims.subject: India Post grievance service standards
claims.applicability: India Post service grievances; not the substantive deceased-account decision.
claims.locator: Citizen Charter, public grievance acknowledgement and settlement rows.

claims.statement: CPGRAMS provides registration-ID-based filing and tracking for eligible Central-government service grievances.
claims.subject: Central grievance
claims.applicability: Eligible Central department service grievances after the responsible route; not succession adjudication.
claims.locator: Portal registration, lodge grievance, status and appeal functions.

claims.statement: CPGRAMS grievances should be redressed within 21 days, and a reasoned interim reply must be given if redress will take longer.
claims.subject: CPGRAMS grievance timeline
claims.applicability: Eligible Central-government service grievances; not court/state succession proceedings.
claims.locator: CPGRAMS FAQ time limit; DARPG 2024 comprehensive guidelines, 21-day redress and interim reply.

claims.statement: A CPGRAMS appeal against an eligible grievance closure must be filed within 30 days.
claims.subject: CPGRAMS appeal period
claims.applicability: Appealable CPGRAMS closures under the current FAQ; not an appeal from a court or substantive inheritance determination.
claims.locator: CPGRAMS FAQ, appeal filing period.

claims.statement: The cited official regimes accept different succession evidence depending on asset, value, nomination, dispute and sector, so no single national legal-heir/probate/succession/notarisation checklist is supported.
claims.subject: Cross-asset succession dependency
claims.applicability: Only the covered regimes; state and court competence remain case specific.
claims.locator: RBI paragraphs 20.1-20.2; SEBI no-nomination bands; NPS regulations 3-4; General Rule 15; IEPF-5 conditional claimant fields.

conflicts.safe_treatment: Use regulation 3(1)(c) and Schedule I Table 1 for the current bands, but still confirm government sector, accumulated pension wealth, claimant capacity and selected option with the responsible intermediary.

conflicts.description: DEA Rule 15 and current India Post guidance align that a no-nomination balance above ₹5 lakh uses a succession certificate. SBI's broader SCSS list is actor- and scheme-specific, not a conflicting nationwide rule.
conflicts.safe_treatment: Use the succession-certificate route for the General Rule/India Post no-nomination >₹5 lakh case; use SBI's broader checklist only for an SBI SCSS account after actor confirmation.
conflicts.resolution_owner_action: The actual account office should confirm scheme/operator and claimant capacity; the claimant must obtain any succession document from the competent forum.

demo_scenario.title: Bounded multi-asset example: Anita inventories Raj's possible assets
demo_scenario.purpose: Demonstrate discovery-first routing across multiple asset classes without treating nomination, a search match or a submission acknowledgement as settlement.
assumptions: Fictional people: Raj is deceased and Anita is his spouse; no real person or account is represented.
A verifiable death certificate exists and matches the known institution records.
No competing claim or court restraint is presently known, but this must be rechecked with each institution.
SBI confirms Anita is the registered nominee on one deposit; a UDGAM search is also run for other DEA-Fund deposits.
A DP confirms Anita is the surviving joint holder of one demat account.
MITRA returns a possible inactive mutual-fund folio with no recorded nomination; AMC value and relationship band remain unconfirmed.
LIC confirms a policy and recorded nomination; product terms, assignment/loan status and benefit remain unconfirmed.
Raj's UAN and employer are known and death occurred while in service, but EPS family/service and EDLI coverage facts still require EPFO/employer confirmation.
A non-government NPS PRAN and recorded nomination are confirmed; the current government-sector amount bands are therefore not used in this example.
A company/folio lead suggests IEPF-held shares, but company/RTA transmission acceptance is not yet complete.
An NSC account lead shows no nomination and an assumed eligible balance of ₹4 lakh; the account office has not yet confirmed the current scheme/form route.

A separate hypothetical postal branch demonstrates the legal-successor gate only: if a General Rule/India Post no-nomination eligible balance were confirmed above ₹5 lakh, a succession certificate would be required, but no state/court process is assumed.

out_of_scope_facts: Whether Anita is the beneficial owner under personal law or must distribute to other heirs
Validity of a will, heirship, state stamp/notarisation practice or court jurisdiction
Tax, estate debts, real property and non-covered financial products
Exact benefit amounts, interest, limitation, fee or completion dates not stated in the cited route
action_required_gates: Bank: confirm nomination, no restraint and complete documents; UDGAM result is only discovery proof.
Mutual fund: AMC/RTA must confirm folio, value, no nomination, spouse relationship and correct QTP/simplified/above-threshold evidence before t.mf-claim.

Insurance: LIC must confirm policy terms, current product form, assignment/loan status and claim; the policy search/acknowledgement is not payment even though IRDAI's 15/45-day and delay-interest controls are verified.

EPFO: confirm establishment, service, family, nomination and coverage separately before Forms 20, 10D and 5IF; do not bundle entitlements. For each claim, retain receipt/completeness evidence because the 20-day payment rule applies only to a claim complete in all respects; retain any deficiency notice and treat 12% interest or penal interest as conditional, not automatic.

NPS: non-government sector and nomination must be institution-confirmed; if actually government sector, confirm accumulated pension wealth and apply the current ₹8 lakh/₹8-12 lakh/above-₹12 lakh Schedule I band, not the stale ₹5 lakh FAQ.

IEPF: company/RTA must confirm original holding and complete applicable SEBI transmission before IEPF-5; SRN and company verification are intermediate only, and the Authority's 60-day clock begins with a complete report.

Postal: account office must confirm NSC rule, no nomination, eligible balance, six-month condition and current Forms 11/13/14/15; assumed ₹4 lakh is not evidence. If the verified General Rule/India Post balance is above ₹5 lakh, stop the simplified route and obtain the succession certificate through the competent case/state/judicial process.
Any competing claimant, will dispute or court restraint stops simplified happy paths and triggers case-specific state/judicial action.
demo_scenario.non_universality_note: This example is deliberately over-specified to exercise multiple branches. Every assumption must be re-proved for the real account, policy, folio, member record, PRAN and scheme. Omit inapplicable branches; never reuse a nominee, threshold, document waiver or succession route across asset classes.
